The 75 bp hike to 3.75–4% and ongoing balance-sheet runoff underscore a still-hawkish, inflation-first stance. The statement’s new emphasis on cumulative tightening and policy lags points to a potential step-down in the pace of future hikes. The latest SLOOS confirms broad tightening in bank credit supply and softer demand across C&I, CRE, residential and consumer lending, with banks citing a weaker outlook and higher recession risk—reinforcing greater caution ahead.

Beige Book (October 2022) reports overall activity flat to modest across districts, with notable housing weakness, mixed consumer spending, and some softening in manufacturing. Labor markets remain tight but show early signs of easing; wage growth is elevated with hints of moderation. Price pressures remain high, though some contacts noted slower increases. These district-level observations align with a more data-dependent posture while inflation risks remain paramount.

Net takeaway: still hawkish, but increasingly constrained by tightening credit conditions and softer activity; bias toward a slower pace rather than a pivot. Adjusting for Beige Book signals of cooling demand and early labor/wage moderation, sentiment is slightly less negative than prior.
